a new, optional load option, agreed with the maintainer: sorted: true writes ids that already ascend one chunk at a time while the object uploads, so a load holds one chunk and the writer's index whatever the segment's size; an id lower than the one before is a ValidationError, and the option is refused with a bitmap input

a new optional method on a backend, agreed with the maintainer: it reports whether the bucket's lifecycle rules would delete or archive the objects the store keeps, in one request (plus the SDK's own retries) and without ever rejecting; a backend without it offers no lifecycle check, and store.preflight() reads that as unchecked, so no implementer or caller has to change
the answer of StorageBackend.checkLifecycle, a status (ok, problem or unchecked) and a sentence for a person; a new type that only the new method returns

S3 implements the optional lifecycle check: one GetBucketLifecycleConfiguration request bounded by readTimeoutMs, a problem for an enabled, untagged rule over the store's prefix that expires current objects or moves them to GLACIER, DEEP_ARCHIVE or a class it does not know, and unchecked, naming s3:GetLifecycleConfiguration, when access is denied

GCS implements the optional lifecycle check: one bucket metadata request bounded by readTimeoutMs, a problem for a Delete rule (or one with an action it does not know) that applies to live objects and can match the store's names, and unchecked, naming storage.buckets.get, when access is denied

Azure Blob implements the optional lifecycle check as always unchecked, with the command that reads the policy by hand: lifecycle policies are on the management plane, out of a blob client's reach, and no management dependency is added
MemoryStorage implements the optional lifecycle check as ok: process memory has no lifecycle rules
LocalFsStorage implements the optional lifecycle check as ok: a local directory has no lifecycle rules

a new store method, agreed with the maintainer: a first-run check that reads the registry, writes, tries to write again, reads, lists and deletes one probe object and asks the backend for its lifecycle verdict; it takes no options and never throws over a finding, only UnsupportedError for a store with no backend
the answer of CloudRoaring.preflight, { ok, checks }, where ok means no check is a problem; a new type that only the new method returns

one check in the answer of CloudRoaring.preflight, { name, status, detail }, with the seven names a literal union in the order a run lists them and a status of ok, problem or unchecked; a new type that only the new method returns
